name: chrome-row-controls
description: The pinned chrome row exists and its four controls act on the VISIBLE tab. The row is sidebar-level, not per-pane - a copy inside a rail pane would scrub away with a swipe, which is the defect the address row was hoisted for. Each control resolves CurrentlyDisplayedWebContents on the C++ side and logs the tab id it landed on, so a control wired to the wrong window or to no window at all is a missing line rather than a silent no-op. The toggle goes LAST: it hides the sidebar, and every eval after it would have no surface to run against.

actions.note: let the space and its tab render. 6s, not 3.5: during startup the window can have more than one sidebar document loading at once, and cdp-eval takes the FIRST target whose url matches - so an eval that lands in that window reads a document whose module graph has not installed yet.

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); if (!row) { return 'no row'; } return [...row.children].map((b) => b.className).join('|'); })()
actions.note: Order is the layout - the row is a flex container and nothing reorders it - so the class list IS the assertion.

actions.expression: (() => { const row = document.querySelector('.sbnav'); const panes = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane')]; if (!row) { return 'no row'; } if (!panes.length) { return 'no rail'; } return panes.some((p) => p.contains(row)) ? 'inside a pane' : 'beside the panes'; })()
actions.note: Guards its own premise: with no rail rendered, 'no rail' fails the assertion rather than passing it vacuously.

actions.expression: (() => { const rows = document.querySelectorAll('.urlrow'); const panes = [...document.querySelectorAll('.railpane')]; if (rows.length !== 1) { return rows.length + ' address rows'; } return panes.some((p) => p.contains(rows[0])) ? 'inside a pane' : 'beside the panes'; })()
actions.note: The reported defect: one address row per pane, all of them translating with the swipe.

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbback'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerdown', {clientX: 8, clientY: 8, bubbles: true})); b.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent('pointerup', {clientX: 8, clientY: 8, bubbles: true})); return 'pressed'; })()
actions.note: down then straight up, well under the hold threshold - a hold asks for the timeline instead

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbfwd'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true})); return 'clicked'; })()
(() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbreload'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true})); return 'clicked'; })()

actions.note: let the reload land before the sidebar is taken away

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbnav .sbtoggle'); if (!b) { return 'no-button'; } b.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true})); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: LAST: this hides the sidebar, so nothing after it can query that surface

assertions.note: The lab's order: the toggle beside the traffic lights, then back, forward, reload (swipe-lab.html:3662). Back carries first, the lab's own right-group anchor.

assertions.label: back-reached-the-visible-tab
assertions.note: The tab id is in the line on purpose: it is the one CurrentlyDisplayedWebContents resolved to, so a control acting on some other window cannot produce it.

assertions.label: toggle-reached-the-window
assertions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar toggle requested from the chrome row
assertions.note: The toggle takes Cmd+S's own path - BrowserController::ToggleSidebar - rather than a second implementation, so there is no tab id to name here.
